text.p: Chaparral Resources Inc said Thursday oil production has been established from the first well to be re-entered in its joint venture development project in the Karakuduk Oil Field in western Kazakhstan.
Produced oil will be trucked to a railhead for transportation and sale. The limited storage tank capacity and winter conditions may delay additional testing and oil sales, the company said.
The well is one of 22 drilled between 1972 and 1992 to delineate the field. None of the wells were placed on production, Chaparral noted.

The re-entered well, No. 21 Karakuduk, flowed from 41 feet of J-1 Jurassic sand between 8,423 and 8,464 feet at a rate of 327 barrels of oil per day on a 12-hour test through a 1/4-inch choke, with flowing tubing pressure 397 pounds per square inch. Natural gas was produced but was not measured. There was no water.

The sand is the upper most of six Jurassic sand pay zones from which the well was originally completed, the company said. The six, with a total of 334 net feet of pay to a depth of 9,950 feet, were production tested in 1992 at a combined rate of 3,131 barrels of oil and 3,087,000 cubic feet of gas per day.
Chaparral said the five remaining pay zones will be tested at a later date, when additional oil storage and upgraded workover equipment have been provided.

The company said additional wells are planned to be reworked and, initially, one new well is scheduled to be drilled. The company estimates it will take the drilling of 90 new oil wells and 26 water injection wells to fully develop the field. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
